intro.text: Agents are ones you make: each is someone you talk to, with optional work it does on its own. deploy.local runs your apps and coding agents on computers you own. Every screen loads the deploy.local design system.

desktop.text: Desktop app: Electron on Mac, Linux and Windows; iOS stays SwiftUI. The window loads deploy.local from your coordinator, trusting only its CA. The shell adds the menu bar or tray, notifications, a login item, the bundled worker (installing the app adds a computer) and the native control helper for screen use. It notifies only for Waiting on you items and failing apps.

cli.text: CLI proposal. Today bin/deploy.js is one 3,389-line file with 35 command lines and 25 global options. Proposed: six groups in the app's words, [app] as an optional positional, steps instead of log dumps, the dark theme's palette, --json everywhere and exit code 3 while something waits on you. Old commands keep working for one release.

build.text: Build rules for v2: the server sends each conversation as typed events (decision, work log, task link, answer, report) and every client renders them, folding but never dropping a decision. Tabs appear only once their thing exists. Words are taught once, where they first happen. Agents answer when you talk to them. Optional background work reports briefly when it finishes or needs a decision.

design-canvas-how.text:
How it works. Designs live in the repo, so any agent (Codex, Claude) or a person can change them on a branch:
• design/canvas.json: sections, board positions, notes
• design/boards/<Name>.html: one self-contained board, styled by the shipped design-system CSS
• design/notes/<Name>.md: what the board is for and the decisions behind it
A visual change is a design change on a branch. Its task gets a Design tab with Before (main) and After (this branch). Approving merges design/ into main, which makes the After the design; then the build task starts. deploy.local renders all of it; no claude.ai needed.

design-canvas-changes.text:
Design: how it works
• Designs live in the repo in design/: canvas.json plus one HTML file per board, built from the design system. Every element has a stable layer ID (data-layer).
• Layout follows Figma: navigation on the left (the d menu with Waiting on you, Designs and the branch, File | Assets, Pages = sections, Layers), the full properties panel on the right, the tool bar at the bottom with vector tools.
• Edits save to a design branch; main changes only through Propose for review and approval (Design tab, chat card, Waiting on you).
• Agents edit through design tools (read, render, structured edits, presence, comments, propose), each on its own branch, shown as a live overlay you accept or discard.
• iPad uses the desktop layout; iPhone has the full canvas with Layers and Edit as sheets.

Build order:
1. Canvas, Layers, Comments, review, and Ask an agent with live editing.
2. Direct edits: text, properties and tokens.
3. Vector tools and Assets.

design-review-notes-how.text: Canvas notes in a proposal use its same plain-language title, proposer summary and decision rules. Open a note by its human title and choose its complete Before or After prose. Never show raw line diffs, layer-edit text or added/removed word fragments. Notes are listed separately from screen thumbnails and do not count toward seen screens. DesignReviewNote / Phone now draw the annotated contact-sheet state; see review-clarity notes.

design-prototype-how.text:
Prototype and Play: how boards connect
• Links already live in the boards: a layer that opens another board carries its link (href). 143 of 171 boards have them.
• Prototype, beside Edit and Comments, draws the selected board's links on the canvas: a line from each layer to the board it opens, the selected layer's line strongest. The repeated sidebar links stay hidden until you show them.
• To see every connection while you move around the canvas, in any tab, turn on Connections in the tool bar (⇧C); see the Connections board.
• With a layer selected, Interaction says what a click does: On click › Go to a board. Change the board, remove the link, or drag the dot at the layer's edge onto a board. Saving writes the layer's link on your design branch, like any edit.
• The board section lists where the board leads and what leads to it; Flow says where Play starts (the page's first board unless you choose another).
• Play (▷, top right) opens the start board full screen and follows links: Back, the trail of boards you passed through, Restart, and the width (1440, 700, 390). Clicking where there's no link lights up the links. Esc or Exit returns to the canvas.
• On iPad, Play is tap to follow, swipe from the left edge to go back, Done to leave.

design-draw-how.text:
Drawing: how it works
• Rectangle, Ellipse and Line (the shape menu, or R, O, L) draw inside a board where you drag. The shape keeps that spot (X and Y) and size, filled surface with a line stroke, and saves to the board on your design branch.
• Text (T): click inside a board to place a text layer and type; Enter keeps it.
• Pen (P): a stroke with Apple Pencil, or a drag, inks a mark on the canvas: danger, W 2.5, the same width on screen at any zoom. Marks sit beside boards like sticky notes, never inside one, and save to canvas.json. Select one to set its rotation, size, opacity, stroke colour, W and Arrow end; drag it to move it; Delete removes it. Tapping points instead draws a vector in a board; Enter, or a tap on the first point, ends it.
• Frame (F): drag on empty canvas to make a new board (Web 1440 or Phone 390 by its width, named Board N until you rename it); inside a board it makes a frame layer.
• Sticky notes (S): click on the canvas; they save to canvas.json and show over the boards they point at. Layers lists a page's marks and sticky notes after its boards.
• Escape goes back to Move (V); the pen keeps inking until you do. Layers drawn in a board can be edited in the properties panel and undone with Reset.

projects-rail-how.text:
One sidebar choice, remembered everywhere on this device
• New devices start with the full 256 px sidebar. Collapse selects the 64 px rail on Projects, Changes, Code and Design alike. There are no page-kind defaults or separate memories.

design-connections-how.text:
Connections: see how boards link without opening Prototype
• Connections, the last button in the tool bar (⇧C, also in the zoom menu), draws every link between boards on the page as an arrow, in Edit, Prototype and Comments alike. It stays on until you turn it off, per person.
• Arrows run board to board, one per pair, however many layers make that link. They're grey and thin so the boards stay readable.
• Select a board and its arrows turn violet: the boards it leads to and the boards that lead to it. Selecting a layer lights only that layer's link.
• Links to boards on other pages don't draw; the board's Connections section lists them under their page. Clicking a row goes to that board.
• Repeated links, like the sidebar on every board, stay hidden; the eye on the Sidebar row draws them too.
• Narrow windows show the same arrows; the Connections section sits in the bottom sheet.

self-update.text: SER is released like any other app, by pushing to its repository. Its update status and recovery pages remain under Computers → deploy.local updates. There is no SER update entry in the sidebar, for administrators or anyone else. The former sidebar status layers now live within those pages. Preparing and activating a SER release still verifies the build, backs up the databases and restores the previous release if health checks fail. Mac app updates are separate and appear only inside the Mac app.

mac-app-update.text:
deploy.local for Mac updates
• Check GET /desktop/version on the coordinator this Mac app is connected to, on launch and every 4 hours. Use its version and short commit, and the darwin-arm64 target’s file, size and sha256. The commit and byte counts on these boards are example data.
• Only the Mac app shows the one-line, nav-height update row, immediately above the account. Details and actions live INSIDE the expanded 256 px sidebar: a popover 8 px directly above the compact row, filling its inner width (about 240 px) with the same 8 px side insets as nav items. Use the design system menu surface, border and shadow; clip the shadow at the sidebar edge so nothing crosses onto the page. At 1440 and 700 px it overlays the lower task list without moving rows, changing list height or changing its scroll position. All update boards include a full task list; actions stack to fit the narrow surface. Pressing the row opens the popover; Escape or an outside click closes it while the download keeps going. It never appears in a browser and never describes SER updating itself. No row when the app is current; a failed background check must not claim it is current.
• Update available opens the popover; Download update starts downloading the published /desktop/ zip. Progress uses actual bytes and total size; Cancel stops and discards the partial download, leaving the installed app unchanged. Downloading 42% rounds 54 of 130 MB.
• After download, show Checking download… in the popover with no actions; the compact row or rail icon shows progress. MacChromeNarrow draws this checking state. Check SHA-256 against the published value before anything changes; only then offer Restart to update. A mismatch leaves the old app untouched and offers Try again. Network errors use “The download stopped. Nothing was changed.” with Try again.
• Restart to update is one press: remember the current page, keep the popover open with a spinner and “Installing… Reopening this page in a moment.” briefly, quit, replace the app in place and reopen on the same coordinator and page. Keep the old app until the new one opens successfully; restore it if installation or launch fails. Do not silently discard the previous app.
• The collapsed rail keeps one download icon above the account, with a small progress or failure glyph and a named tooltip. Pressing it temporarily expands the sidebar to 256 px and opens the same in-sidebar popover, without starting Download or Restart. This expansion never changes the remembered sidebar choice. MacChromeNarrow draws the temporary expanded checking state; DesignMac shows the closed failed icon and follows the same behavior. Escape, an outside click, pressing the update row again, Collapse, Later or the quiet Dismiss action close details; if opened from the rail, collapse back to 64 px and return focus to the download icon. A download or check continues and its icon remains available to reopen details. If opened from an already expanded sidebar, closing details leaves it expanded. Preserve the task list’s scroll position throughout; resizing or changing update state while details are open does not save an expanded preference.
• The install handoff and restoring the same page require implementation verification after this design is approved; these are static review boards.

design-review-compare.text: At 1440, changed screens show labelled Before and After side by side at equal scale. At 700 and on iPhone use the Before/After toggle. decision-content.text: A decision shows what it is about: an agent's question shows the reply it refers to (the agent's latest message in the task), a merge shows its diff, a release what ships. Names, never IDs. Nothing that looks pressable is inert: no sample suggestions, no empty-state cards that repeat the composer. An empty Today has no section header. Waiting rows show the agent’s name and reply preview, never its ID.

question-decision-behavior.text: QuestionDecision / QuestionDecisionPhone: the draft is the agent's latest reply in this decision's task, rendered as markdown above every answer action. Scroll the bordered preview to read the full supplied reply; Open the task opens that task's whole conversation. Show “Scroll to read more” only when the content is taller than its block: omit it on the web board where everything fits, keeping Open the task right-aligned, and keep it on the phone board where the content overflows. A design decision shows its boards. Empty and whitespace-only answers keep Answer disabled; entering text enables it. Web: 1440 and 700 px. iPhone sheet: 390 px. Asked 12m ago is an example relative time.

new-agent-phone.text:
New agent is a name and an avatar; you teach it in the chat; details and Looks after items live behind its name.
• + in the web sidebar or the iPhone Agents header opens NewAgentBlank / NewAgentBlankPhone; NewAgent / NewAgentPhone show a filled name after an avatar choice. Only avatar, Shuffle, color, Name and Create. No templates, generated draft, purpose, access, approvals or schedule in creation. Blank or whitespace-only names disable Create; trim on save. Creation failures keep the entered name and chosen avatar for retry.
• Create opens AgentHello / AgentHelloPhone: a big avatar, name, “Tell <name> what you want it to do. It remembers.” and four suggested first messages. Tapping a suggestion fills the composer for editing; it sends only when you press Send. No invented greeting, task, Looks after item or history. All five action rules initially Ask.
• The name/avatar in the chat header opens AgentSettings / AgentInfoPhone. Edit the avatar, color and name; What it does reflects what it learned from your messages and can be edited. Save keeps these changes; closing without Save preserves the saved version. Phone editing is supported here, not deferred to a computer.
• Looks after is optional and initially empty: “Nothing to look after yet” and Add. AgentRoutine and AgentBeatProjects (+Phone) share a web dialog / iPhone sheet. Fields in order: What; Where (All Active / All Active and Maintained / Chosen projects, revealing a stage/access checklist); When (Every week / Every day / On each change, day, time, On SER’s clock); Brings (A pull request / A design review / A question / A message); Confirm item / Cancel. Scheduled work starts only after confirmation; save never runs it immediately. Both fixtures use Confirm item / Cancel. AgentRuns (+Phone) shows History under one item and Run now.
• Phone sheets scroll between the pinned header and action, resize above the keyboard, keep the focused field visible and respect safe areas. Touch targets are at least 44 px. The ten color choices wrap into two rows of five on iPhone; on web they form one row. The owner will render 1440/700/390 and commit; this branch contains design only.

settings-phone-behavior.text:
iPhone Settings · nothing that looks pressable is inert
• Account is identity, with no link or chevron.
• Notification settings and Paired devices are full-width rows with chevrons. They open the existing V2NotificationSettings and V2DevicesView sheets; these static boards specify those native destinations with data-destination.
• What agents may do opens SettingsApprovalsPhone. Done dismisses it back to Settings. Each agent’s rules are plain, read-only action/value rows: Ask, Allowed or Never. No editable chips, switches or chevrons. Change these in Settings on a computer.
• SettingsAgents and SettingsApprovalsPhone show all five saved agents. Release notes writer: Start a task Allowed, the other four actions Ask. Ops watcher, Code reviewer, Researcher and Designer: all five actions Ask in the shared settings snapshot. The agent list comes from the coordinator; no built-ins. Creation defaults every action to Ask without an approvals step. This Settings sheet remains read-only, with changes made on a computer. When opened from agent details, Done returns to those details; from Settings, it returns to Settings.
• Backups opens the existing restore sheet (RestorePhone); its copy stays “Restore to a copy”.
• Appearance opens a menu: System (selected), Light, Dark. Choosing a value immediately applies and remembers this iPhone’s appearance preference; System follows iOS.
• Screen use, removing data and secrets stay on a computer. This is a plain footnote under the groups.
• The settings list scrolls above a full-width, centered destructive Sign out button at the bottom. Sign out uses the existing sign-out flow. No app implementation changes in this design pass.
• Team limits is a separate editable section on iPhone. Existing per-action permission rows remain read-only. Archive is immutable Always asks, outside the five action selectors.

chat-agents-model.text:
Agents are conversations first — approved direction; additions for review
• New agent is a name and an avatar; you teach it in the chat; details and Looks after items live behind its name. No built-in agents and no templates. The fixture has five saved agents: Release notes writer (variant28, af61f2), Ops watcher (variant21, 2fb5a3), Code reviewer (variant29, 76a7ff), Researcher (variant10, ffaa64), Designer (variant03, e66bb8); the 35 picker glyphs are avatar choices, not saved agents.
• Avatars are DiceBear Glyphs (@dicebear/core 10 + @dicebear/styles, bundled, drawn offline): one of 35 glyphs plus one color, never a random photo. One color draws the whole avatar: a tinted circle, the glyph and darker shoulders. An agent stores its glyph and color; a new agent starts with a random glyph and color picked when the dialog opens (blank fixture: variant07, ff4d6f). Typing a name never changes its glyph; Shuffle and Choose avatar do. Glyphs is CC BY 4.0 by Matt Houser (a remix of “Abstract Avatars for All Creative Profile Use”): credit him in Settings → General (Credits at the bottom).
• AvatarPicker boards show the state reached by tapping the large avatar in creation or details. All 35 glyphs show in the current color, the chosen one outlined. The current example is Release notes writer as glyph 28 in Violet everywhere: list, chat, task mention and approvals. Selection keeps the current color; a swatch keeps the current drawing; Shuffle picks a glyph/color pair. Done returns to the invoking surface, preserving the Name and all other edits. Cancel restores the prior avatar. The picker is shared by creation and details, not another creation step.
• Ten colors: Violet #af61f2, Blue #76a7ff, Green #75c675, Amber #e8b130, Red #ff4d6f, Indigo #525fa3, Teal #2fb5a3, Orange #ffaa64, Pink #e66bb8, Gray #8c8c8c (Glyphs' own palette plus four). These are identity colors, never status indicators; status keeps its own icon and label.
• Open an agent to its conversation. Ordinary answers stay prose. Requested work appears as an attributed linked task. Sidebar and Work rows show avatar, name, last message and time. An empty conversation says Say hello with no fabricated timestamp. No agents keeps the + and the invitation to make one. The web sidebar folds below 820 px; chat, details and dialogs remain usable at 700 px.
• AgentSettings / AgentInfoPhone and AgentCareDetails / AgentCareDetailsPhone share one details layout: page on web, sheet on iPhone. In order: avatar, Change avatar, Shuffle, colors; Name; editable What it does; What it’s learned; Looks after; Stopped suggestions only when nonempty (Code reviewer has one; Release notes writer has none); What it may use; Approvals summary; Delete. What it does updates from explicit instructions in chat; it is not a generated pre-creation draft. New agents begin with no learned purpose and no Looks after items. No per-agent connected-app setup: connections belong to the account and are managed in account settings. Project and computer access still applies to each agent.
• TaskMention / TaskMentionPhone keep @ in the composer: only saved agents are offered, filtered by name. Select inserts a stable @Name reference; sending delivers it. Arrow keys, Enter and Escape work on web. No match says No matching agents; no agents offers New agent. The picker stays above the keyboard. Mentions do not expand resource access or bypass approvals.
• Agents may message other saved agents: use the same identity and attributed-message model, surface the sender and recipient, keep their replies in the originating conversation, and apply each agent’s own access and approval rules. no autonomous message loops or automatic schedules implied by a mention.
• Looks after is one list of saved items: what, where, when and brings. Draft release notes · home-gym · Fridays 16:00 · brings a message uses the same editor as Code quality and updates. AgentTaught shows the pending schedule; AgentRoutine reviews it. AgentPage and AgentRuns show the later confirmed item and History. No history means no run is claimed.
• The current chat/task bridge still needs approval-aware task creation, structured mention recipients and enforced resource scope. Retain the five Ask / Allowed / Never actions and the connected model/default. Saved legacy apps/trigger values must survive an eventual migration; removing their controls is not permission to erase them. No implementation, merge, push or release is part of this branch.
• Teaching in chat updates What it does and shows “Now looks after: … · Confirm · Edit”. Confirm is the primary inline receipt action; Edit opens the shared item editor. After confirmation the receipt reads “Confirmed · first check <day> <time> · Edit”. It never silently starts a schedule.
• NewAgentBlank / NewAgentBlankPhone are the immediate + state: empty Name with placeholder, visibly disabled Create (aria-disabled). NewAgent / NewAgentPhone remain filled examples after choosing the violet glyph. Name-only edits preserve the random avatar. Picker Done returns to its invoking state and keeps the name.
• Saved-agent list links carry the selected agent identity; query examples reuse the chat layout with that agent’s name, glyph, color and history. The drawn chat and details fixtures remain Release notes writer. Ops incident/report and Release notes writer long-history boards are examples of owner-created agents with access and confirmed Looks after schedules, never built-ins. The five-agent list previews represent the shared current snapshot, independent of historical or creation-state examples.
• Confirm item saves the schedule and returns an inline “Confirmed · first check Friday 16:00 · Edit” receipt. Code reviewer’s first check is Monday 08:40. No runs yet. Run now is separate. Existing items use the same editor with Confirm item / Cancel.
• Looks after items prepare small work within team limits and action rules; the care flow defines PR, design-review and ask-first decisions. There is no separate inspection-only kind. Designer’s last message remains “Proposed a calmer Tally header.” · Tue.

project-care-model.text:
Your agents look after your projects
• Flow: make an agent → teach it what to look after → it brings work → you decide (merge / approve design / ask first) → weekly summary → archive → limits. Use existing navigation.
• Agents are owner-created: Code reviewer, Researcher, Designer (fifth agent, Glyphs), Ops watcher and Release notes writer. One Looks after item stores what, where, when and what it brings: PR, design review, question or message. Add opens chat or the editor. Teaching shows “Now looks after: … · Confirm · Edit”; Confirm is the primary inline action and Edit opens the shared item editor. History belongs to the item; confirmation never runs it immediately.
• Scope intersects granted access and stage; teaching grants no access. Only the owner changes stage. Active accepts all kinds; Maintained accepts Fix/Update only; Done accepts no work or checks. Moving to Maintained withdraws incompatible proposals and pauses incompatible work. Visible Fix/Update work requires design review, including on Maintained.
• Inside the size cap, Fix/Update/Improvement work is prepared on a branch within saved action rules. Its proposal is the PR: evidence revision/source, changed files, tests, passing checks, size and project. Merge: Ask is satisfied by Merge; Allowed follows its saved rule; Never shows “You merge this one” and a PR link, without an agent-merge button. Ask for changes opens that agent’s PR conversation. how-agents-learn.text:
How agents learn
• Three layers of context: lessons live per agent on SER; project knowledge lives in the project’s repository AGENTS.md or design/ notes, changed through a pull request; run history lives on SER and includes reports, answers and outcomes.
• Every run receives, in order: the job (What it does); lessons that apply to this project; the project’s AGENTS.md; the last report; recent outcomes of its own proposals (merged / closed + optional reason / changes asked / edits before merge as a diffstat). Preserve source links and project identity.
• Record outcomes for every proposal and pull request the agent brings. Reasons are optional. Owner answers include Close with a reason, Ask for changes, edits before merging, Stop suggesting this, and explicit chat instructions.
• Nothing inferred is kept without the owner’s Keep it. Inferred patterns bring a Learning proposal with evidence and a before/after instruction diff. Edit changes the proposal and returns to Keep it; Save in that editor does not keep it. Close frees its slot without adding a lesson. Learning reserves a proposal slot like any other and does not consume a project PR budget.
• Explicit instructions save immediately with a visible, undoable receipt: “Learned: Keep pull requests under about 100 lines · Edit · Undo”. Teaching the job remains What it does; learned preferences belong in What it’s learned. An explicit project convention still goes through the project-knowledge PR flow.
• Every lesson shows its source. Source links open the original answer, PR or chat message. The owner can edit or remove any lesson, and choose All projects or Chosen projects. LessonEdit shows one existing lesson; #explicit shows its chat source; #proposal edits an inferred proposal before Keep it. Other lesson links carry agent and lesson identity to the same editor layout. Changes affect future runs; removal and Keep it have Undo.
• At most 20 lessons per agent. The limit stops only lessons it worked out itself: what you tell it directly always saves, even past 20. Over the limit, it brings a Learning proposal that combines lessons and waits for Keep it; it never silently deletes or combines lessons. Do not claim “Learned” until storage succeeds. Lessons never grant access or widen approval rules; selected scope intersects current access.
• Project facts, such as tally’s lowercase header and buttons, are Improvement proposals with a ready AGENTS.md diff and PR. Merge / Ask for changes / Close follow the normal care flow. Owner preferences remain per agent, not in the repository. Design/ knowledge follows design approval rules as well.
• Server work needed: a lesson store with text, project scope and linked sources; outcome records for proposals and PRs; Learning proposal kind; prompt assembly in the order above; project-knowledge PRs through the normal care flow; idempotent answers and undo receipts. Keep suppressions distinct from inferred lessons: Stop suggesting this takes effect immediately for that finding, but any broader inferred lesson needs Keep it.
• New-agent details show “Nothing learned yet. It learns from how you answer its work.” Existing shared details show lessons between What it does and Looks after. Reports and weekly summaries only claim a lesson after it was saved or kept.
• Review widths: web 1440 and 700, iPhone 390. Owner renders and commits; this change is design only.
• Prototype states are navigable with fragments: ProposalLearning#kept and #undone; AgentLearned#undone; LessonEdit#proposal and #explicit; ProposalFix#closed-too-big (and each other reason). The editor’s typed value and selected projects are illustrative static fields; the implementation must carry draft edits back into the proposal diff before Keep it. Saving an existing lesson or removing one never changes the job text.

These are static design fixtures; HTML links identify destinations, not implemented review logic. Phone notes supersede the old phone-specific grid/toggle language in shared review notes. Web/Mac layout stays unchanged; drawing-pin display follows the drawing contract below.

Compare and paging: the toolbar order is Compare, pencil (Draw and comment), Show changes, width chip. All hit targets are at least 44 px and remain on one line at 390 px; Seen / pins moves to the quiet line below. All screens and Place a pin remain in ⋯. Compare enters a full-preview wipe, not a slider below the image or an opacity blend. Before is left, After right, with nonwrapping capsules; the divider is drawn at 40%. Both revisions share the same scale, native crop and pan. One-finger dragging anywhere on the preview moves the divider and never pages. Two fingers pan / pinch both revisions together. Done or tapping Compare again exits and restores paging at the same crop. Do not carry compare mode into another screen. VoiceOver exposes the divider as an adjustable control (Before percentage); hardware arrow keys adjust it. Compare and draw modes are mutually exclusive.
Gestures: retain press-and-hold as a shortcut on the Compare control: hold shows all Before, release restores the prior After or divider position without also firing a tap. Long-press on the preview stays a pin gesture; it cannot also trigger Before. Outside compare/draw, horizontal swipes page at the initial crop; when zoomed, pan within the screen and return to the initial crop to page. Long-press or ⋯ → Place a pin opens the existing pin sheet; the explicit action is the accessible alternative. In compare mode, long-press creates no pin. In draw mode, one finger always draws; long-press neither compares nor creates another pin.

Compare is visibly disabled with “No Before for this screen” (drawn in DesignReviewNewPhone); a Removed screen is Before only, disabled with “No After for this screen”. Show changes is disabled when no revision pair exists. Pencil and long-press can comment on the available revision, including removal. Preserve the width chip; a single available width is informational, multiple widths open a menu. Never fabricate a baseline. Width changes leave compare mode and retain each width’s crop; an unfinished drawing must be finished or cancelled first.
Pencil: entering draw mode stops paging and freezes the selected board/revision/width. One finger draws freehand; two fingers pan/zoom without adding a stroke. One accent stroke, 3 native px with round caps and joins; no colour picker. Undo removes the last completed stroke (including the arrow as one stroke), disabled when empty. Next is disabled until a stroke exists. Cancel discards the drawing and returns to the originating page/crop without adding a pin. Next opens the native comment sheet with a crop thumbnail of the drawn area, Cancel / Comment / Add, and the focused “What should change?” field. Add is disabled until trimmed text is nonempty. Sheet Cancel returns to drawing with strokes and draft text retained; only drawing Cancel discards them. Dismissing the sheet behaves like Cancel. Add saves the text and all strokes together as one numbered pin, dismisses the sheet and leaves draw mode. A failed save retains the draft and offers Retry; it never increments the count.
Drawing storage and web: store paths with the pin as normalized native-board coordinates (x / board width, y / board height), not viewport or crop coordinates. Associate proposal revision, board ID, Before/After side, width variant, native dimensions, normalized anchor, ordered strokes and stroke weight. Transform paths and anchor together during crop, pan, zoom and scrubbing; clip them to the associated revision side. Keep the original revision/width association across updates, never stretch a path onto another width or silently move it to a new revision. All strokes in one saved drawing count as one unresolved pin in Ask for N changes, exactly like a point pin. Show changes controls the region outlines and saved pins/drawings together; turning it off hides both anchor and paths. A visible or selected pin reveals its strokes. Tapping its number opens the text and drawing for inspection, edit or removal. Deleting the pin deletes its paths; addressed pins remain inspectable. Web and Mac display the same normalized paths in the corresponding revision/width preview and the same numbered pin and text in their existing pins tray; no new desktop toolbar is proposed.
Loading and motion: use skeletons in the real preview layout until the requested revision/width is ready; after 10 seconds say “Screen preview is taking longer than usual.” Do not enable Compare until both images are ready, or draw/pin until the visible image is ready. Preserve the existing decision-loading and conflict rules. Divider and strokes track the finger directly, without easing or replay. app-requests.text:
Requests
Web app
iPhone: later

Only web apps (an app with an address) get the Requests tab; workers keep Overview and Settings. Numbers come from the 1-minute rollups; the list reads request_logs (90 days). Bodies are saved for server errors only (14 days, at most 30 a minute per app). Rows in the summaries open the list filtered to that path; a list row opens the request.

In a one-app project the app is the project page, so Requests is a project tab after Releases (OneAppProject). It opens the same page as AppRequests under the project’s tabs. Workers never get it.

States the boards do not draw: a server error with nothing saved (over 30 a minute, or older than 14 days) shows What was sent with “Not saved. deploy.local saves up to 30 server errors a minute for each app and keeps them for 14 days.” and no What came back. A range with no requests reads “No requests in 24 hours” in Slowest paths and the list, and “No server errors” in Most server errors. Logs opens the app’s logs; they cannot jump to a time yet.

packages-how.text:
Proposal. deploy.local hosts npm packages and Cargo crates, and keeps a copy of everything projects install from npmjs.org and crates.io, so installs keep working when those sites are down.

• Packages sits in the sidebar under Computers. It appears once deploy.local has served a package: a private one, or a copy. On approval, every board's sidebar gets the same row.
• Tabs: Private, Copies, Set up. A package opens its page: install, versions, the projects that use it (read from each project's lockfile on main).
• Versions are never replaced or deleted. npm versions can be deprecated and crates yanked from the package page's version rows.
• Who publishes: pipelines, so nobody has to release a package by hand. deploy.yaml's pipeline gets a publish list. Once every job passes on main, each listed package whose version is new is published (PipelineRun), and a version already published is skipped. A failed publish fails the run, and Run pipeline retries it. Merging a new version is what starts it (TaskPublish). Pull requests never publish. People can still run deploy packages publish, for a package with no pipeline. Tasks and agents never publish; their computers' keys only install. There is no publish card in Waiting on you.
• A project with a pipeline shows Pipelines after Apps, as the app has today. This board is the first to draw that tab.
• Copies tab, normal state: no banner, both sources read Reachable, Packages kept has one row for all projects, and the sidebar row shows nothing. While a source is down the sidebar shows Using copies, as drawn. Only projects with a problem get their own row, with the cause. A missing package is fetched on its own when the source is back. A version its source removed stops installing until the project moves off it.
• Copies cover npm packages and crates. App builds also need their Docker image, which deploy.local doesn't keep.
• Package keys (Settings, General) are made by deploy packages login from your CLI sign-in. Installs only or Installs and publishes. Remove revokes it at once.
• Project settings get a Packages group with one switch, Install through deploy.local (on). A project with packages gets a Packages tab after Releases, listing its own packages with the same rows.
• Mac app: the window loads these web pages; nothing native is added. iPhone: Settings → Packages is read-only (PackagesPhone). Rows open the package's versions in a sheet.

project-remove-failed.text:
Removing a project reports success only when nothing is left. If it could not finish, the dialog stays open, the project stays, and the error says why. Pressing Remove project again picks up where it stopped.

The same banner carries the other cases:
• The computer running this app is offline.
• This app still has instances on [site], out of reach.
• This computer needs a newer worker to confirm the app is gone. Update it, then retry removal.
• The computer could not remove the app: [reason].
• Still waiting for the computer to remove the app. Retry removal to check again.

Docker not running (server/v2/project-removal.ts): use the existing danger banner, with the dialog open, confirmation retained and Remove project available. “Docker isn't running on this computer, so nothing was removed. Start it, then press Remove project.” deploy.local keeps the project and waits for you to retry; it does not announce success or auto-remove anything when Docker starts. Raw connect ENOENT /Users/…/docker.sock belongs in Logs, never in the banner. ProjectRemoveFailed keeps its partial-removal example. Docker uses the same layout, so no additional error state is drawn. This “nothing was removed” wording applies when Docker was unavailable before any removal. If some work already completed, keep the existing partial-removal case, naming what remains, and say Docker must be started before pressing Remove project again. Never claim untouched data after partial removal.

Existing partial-removal banner (still drawn here): “Removal is not finished. Still on this machine: deploy-sh-home-gym-web-1, deploy-sh-home-gym-default. Press Remove project to try again.”

App count controls the wording on web and Mac/Windows/Linux desktop. Names below are fixture names; use the actual app names and count, never guess while the list is loading. Keep backup retention and release guidance as separate existing sentences.
• One app — dialog: “This would stop home-gym and free its addresses.” Settings row: “Stops the app and frees its addresses.”
• Two apps — dialog: “This would stop home-gym and home-gym-sync and free their addresses.” Settings row: “Stops the apps and frees their addresses.” For more apps, list their actual names with the existing list formatting and keep plural wording.
• No apps — dialog: “This project has no apps to stop or addresses to free.” Settings row: “Removes the project. There are no apps to stop or addresses to free.” Removal still requires the project-name confirmation and preserves the existing backup-retention behavior.

The same dialog and Settings row layouts cover all three counts; no additional boards or product implementation in this proposal.

backup-drive-missing.text:
A backup never writes to a drive that is not there. If the drive is missing, nothing is copied, so it cannot fill the computer’s own disk.

The same banner carries the other cases:
• Backup destination [path] has no .deploy-backup-destination file, so it may be an empty mount point on this computer’s own disk. Nothing was written. If the drive is not mounted, mount it.
• Backup destination [path] overlaps the data directory [path]. Nothing was written.
• Database snapshots need [size] free on the data disk at [path], and it has [size]. Nothing was copied.
• Backup destination [path] ran out of space, so this copy is incomplete.
• Backup destination [path] can’t make hard links, so it can’t keep dated copies. Nothing was written. Format the drive as ext4.
• Backup destination [path] doesn’t have room for this copy, which needs [size]. Nothing was written.
